record.title: Conjecture on feedback arc sets in 3-free digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite digraph with no parallel edges, and call $G$ **3-free** if it has no directed cycle of length at most $3$. Let $\gamma(G)$ be the number of unordered pairs $\{u,v\}$ of distinct nonadjacent vertices of $G$ (that is, neither $uv$ nor $vu$ belongs to $E(G)$), and let $\beta(G)$ be the minimum cardinality of a set $X\subseteq E(G)$ such that $G\setminus X$ is acyclic. The conjecture is that every 3-free digraph satisfies
\[
\beta(G)\le \frac{1}{2}\gamma(G).
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1532), page 9. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Threshold for online vertex colorings of random graphs
record.statement: Determine, for a fixed graph $F$ and $r$ available colors, the threshold $p_0(F,r,n)$ for the online vertex-coloring game on $G_{n,p}$: vertices are revealed one at a time together with all edges induced by the vertices revealed so far, and Painter must immediately color each vertex without creating a monochromatic copy of $F$. Specifically, determine for which values of $p$ Painter can a.a.s. color the entire graph, in the sense that she succeeds a.a.s. when $p\ll p_0$ and every strategy fails a.a.s. when $p\gg p_0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1536), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Lusztig’s conjecture for split even-dimensional special orthogonal groups in characteristic 2
record.statement: Determine the scalars occurring in Lusztig’s conjecture for the finite split special orthogonal groups $G^F=\operatorname{SO}_{2n}(\mathbb{F}_q)^F$ when the characteristic is $p=2$, i.e. determine the roots of unity $\zeta_x$ such that $\chi_{A_x,\varphi_x}=\zeta_xR_x$ under the parametrization of $F$-stable character sheaves by almost characters. The report states that the method used for $\operatorname{Sp}_{2n}$ is expected to apply to the split-type $\operatorname{SO}_{2n}$ case, which was under progress; it does not apply to the non-split type.

record.title: Accessory parameter problem in positive characteristic
record.statement: Let $k=\bar{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$, let $X=\mathbf{P}^1_k$, and choose a parameter $t$ on $X$. Consider differential operators $L=\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\right)^2+p_1\frac{\partial}{\partial t}+p_2$, with $p_1,p_2\in k(t)$, regular singularities at $x_1,\ldots,x_r=\infty$, and local exponents $(0,0)$ at $x_i$ for $i\ne r$ and $(r/2-1,r/2-1)$ at $x_r=\infty$. Define $N_{0,r}$ to be the space of such operators having a polynomial solution, and $N_{0,r}[d]\subset N_{0,r}$ to be the subspace for which the minimal degree of a polynomial solution is $d$. Determine the structure of $N_{0,r}$ and $N_{0,r}[d]$.

record.title: Minimum and uniqueness of one-dimensional phase-boundary fronts
record.statement:
Let $F:\mathbb{R}\to\braket{0,+\infty}$ be continuous and strictly positive except at $m=a$ and $m=b$, where $a<b$. Let
\[
\mathcal{C}_{a,b}=\left\{m:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}:\lim_{x\to-\infty}m(x)=a,\ \lim_{x\to+\infty}m(x)=b\right\},
\]
and define
\[
\mathcal{F}(m)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}F(m(x))\,dx+\frac12\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(m(x)-m(y))^2J(x-y)\,dx\,dy,
\]
where $J$ is a non-negative integrable function on $\mathbb{R}$. Determine the minimum of $\mathcal{F}$ over $\mathcal{C}_{a,b}$ and whether the minimizing profiles are unique up to translation.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1544), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Subexponentiality of the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem over extension fields
record.statement: There exists some $c>0$ such that the following holds: the discrete logarithm problem in $E(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$, where $n\le c\log(q)$ and $E$ is any elliptic curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, can be solved in an expected time which is polynomial in $q$. Here the discrete logarithm problem is: given $P,Q\in E(\mathbb{F}_{q^n})$ with $Q\in\langle P\rangle$, find some $x\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $Q=x\cdot P$.

record.title: The fair-duel problem for a universal ordering
record.statement:
Given a sequence $q=(q_n)_{n\ge 0}$ with $q_n\in\{-1,+1\}$, where $q$ specifies whose turn it is in the duel, and where each shot independently hits with an unknown but fixed probability $\varepsilon\le \tfrac12$, find a universal ordering $q$, independent of $\varepsilon$, that is as fair as possible. Writing
\[
B_q(\varepsilon):=\mathbb P\{A\text{ survives}\}-\mathbb P\{B\text{ survives}\}
=\varepsilon\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(1-\varepsilon)^n,
\]
seek an ordering for which $B_q(\varepsilon)\to 0$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ as fast as possible.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2007/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1592), page 27. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Exact projected convolution of hp-functions on locally refined grids
record.statement: Given bounded-support functions $f\in S^f$ and $g\in S^g$, compute the exact function $\omega=P(f*g)$, where $(f*g)(x)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(y)g(x-y)\,dy$ and $P$ is the $L^2(\mathbb R)$-orthogonal projection onto a prescribed hp-space $S^\omega\subset L^2(\mathbb R)$. The spaces are formed from locally refined, piecewise-polynomial bases consisting of affine images of normalized Legendre polynomials on mesh intervals $I^\ell_i=[ih_\ell,(i+1)h_\ell)$, with the three spaces allowed to have different refinement zones (and, according to the footnote, possibly different local polynomial degrees).

record.title: Dimension of the tautological ring of a general Jacobian
record.statement: Let $C$ be a general smooth irreducible curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$, let $J$ be its Jacobian, and let $R$ be the smallest subring of $A(J)=CH^*_{\mathbb Q}(J)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{alg}}$ containing the class $[C]$ and stable under the intersection product, Pontryagin product, the action of $\mathbb Z\subset\operatorname{End}(J)$, and the Fourier–Mukai transform. If $p(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$, is $\dim_{\mathbb Q}R=p(g+1)$?

record.title: NP-completeness of the Rank Decoding problem
record.statement: Can one find a reduction proving that the following Rank Decoding (RD) problem is NP-complete? Given $N,n,k\in\mathbb{N}^*$, a generator matrix $G\in M_{k\times n}(\mathbb{F}_{q^N})$, a received word $c\in\mathbb{F}_{q^N}^n$, and $r\in\mathbb{N}^*$, decide whether there exists $m\in\mathbb{F}_{q^N}^k$ such that $e=c-mG$ satisfies $\operatorname{rank}(e\mid\mathbb{F}_q)\le r$, where $\operatorname{rank}(e\mid\mathbb{F}_q)$ is the rank of the $N\times n$ matrix representing $e$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.

record.title: Independent-neighborhood hypergraphs for uniformities 5 and 6
record.statement: For $n\ge k\ge 2$, let $f(n,k)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph whose neighborhoods of all $(k-1)$-sets are independent. Call a $k$-graph odd if its vertex set has a partition $X\cup Y$ such that every edge contains an odd number of vertices of $Y$, fewer than $k$. Let $B(n,k)$ be an odd $k$-graph on $n$ vertices with the maximum possible number of edges, and let $b(n,k)=|B(n,k)|$. The conjecture is that $f(n,k)=b(n,k)$ for $k\in\{5,6\}$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

record.title: Box-distance between symmetric and monotone distributions
record.statement: Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be distributions on the product set $S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_k$. Define their box-distance as the maximum of $\lvert D_1(A)-D_2(A)\rvert$ over boxes $A=A_1\times\cdots\times A_k$, where $A_i\subseteq S_i$. A distribution $D$ on $k$-tuples of integers is called monotone if $D(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=0$ unless $x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_k$, and symmetric if $D(x_1,\ldots,x_k)=D(y_1,\ldots,y_k)$ whenever $(y_1,\ldots,y_k)$ is a permutation of $(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$. What is the minimum box-distance between a symmetric distribution and a monotone distribution on $k$-tuples of integers from $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1782), page 60. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Finite-horizon optimal portfolio liquidation for CARA investors
record.statement:
Given an initial position $x>0$ and a finite or infinite horizon $T\in[0,\infty]$, let $\mathcal X(x,T)$ be the class of bounded, predictable, absolutely continuous liquidation strategies $X$ satisfying $X_0=x$ and $X_T=0$. Under the Almgren price-impact model, with $P_0,\gamma>0$, $b,\sigma\in\mathbb R$, a standard Brownian motion $B$ with $B_0=0$, and $f(y):=yh(y)$ positive, strictly convex, continuously differentiable, and of superlinear growth, define
$$
R_T(X)=R_0+\sigma\int_0^T X_s\,dB_s+b\int_0^T X_s\,ds+\int_0^T f(\dot X_s)\,ds,
\qquad R_0=P_0x-\frac{\gamma}{2}x^2.
$$
For CARA utility $u(r)=-e^{-\alpha r}$ with $\alpha>0$, determine the strategy solving
$$
\max_{X\in\mathcal X(x,T)}\mathbb E\!\left[-e^{-\alpha R_T(X)}\right].
$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/04](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1785), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Statistics of zeros in the local regime for hyperelliptic-curve zeta functions
record.statement: For a fixed odd prime power $q$, let $\mathcal H_{2g+2,q}$ be the family of curves $C:y^2=Q(x)$ over $\mathbb F_q$, where $Q$ is monic, square-free, and has degree $2g+2$. If $\theta_{C,j}$ are the $2g$ eigenangles of the unitarized Frobenius class and $N_I(C)=\#\{j:\theta_{C,j}\in I\}$, determine the fluctuations of $N_I(C)$ as $g\to\infty$ in the local regime, when the interval length is of order $1/(2g)$.

record.title: First-principles derivation of the AdResS force-interpolation formula
record.statement:
Derive the AdResS force-interpolation formula from first principles of statistical mechanics,
\[
F_{\alpha\beta}=w(X_\alpha)w(X_\beta)F^{\mathrm{atom}}_{\alpha\beta}+\bigl[1-w(X_\alpha)w(X_\beta)\bigr]F^{\mathrm{cm}}_{\alpha\beta},
\]
where $w$ is the molecular switching function, $X_\alpha$ and $X_\beta$ are molecular center-of-mass coordinates, and the two forces are respectively the atomistic and coarse-grained center-of-mass forces. In particular, formally determine the latent heat $\phi$ associated with changing resolution, so that the thermostat used to maintain equilibrium can be removed and the method made internally consistent, possibly through an explicit generalized thermodynamical potential.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1966), page 29. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Global-in-time behavior of small two-dimensional water waves
record.statement: Determine the global-in-time behavior of solutions of the two-dimensional, infinite-depth water-wave system (1) for small initial data, where the fluid is incompressible and irrotational, gravity is present, and surface tension is zero. The report states that this question remains open; it proves only an almost-global result, with existence up to times of order $e^{T/\varepsilon}$ for sufficiently small data.

record.title: Functional equation for ideal reduced zeta functions
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}[[t]]$ with a nice and simple basis $B=\{x_1,\ldots,x_d\}$. Let $0=Z_0\le Z_1\le\cdots\le Z_c=L$ be its upper central series, and let $h_i$ be the smallest number such that $x_i\in Z_{h_i}$. Define $x_l\prec x_i$ if there exists $j$ such that $[x_i,x_j]=a x_l$ with $a\ne0$, and extend $\prec$ transitively. If, whenever $x_l\prec x_i$ and $h_i>h_l+1$, there exists $r$ such that $x_l\prec x_r\prec x_i$, then
$$R^{\triangleleft}_L(T^{-1})=(-1)^dT^{\sum_{i=1}^d h_i}R^{\triangleleft}_L(T).$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1973), page 19. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: A Wilks phenomenon for bounded contrast minimization
record.statement: In settings beyond the classical parametric likelihood framework, does the increment of a centered empirical process between a fixed point and a random point exhibit a non-trivial yet understandable behavior? The report investigates this question for bounded contrast minimization problems, in particular for the empirical excess risk $Z=n\bigl(R_n(\bar f)-R_n(\hat f)\bigr)$ arising from a statistical-learning problem with sampling distribution $P$ on $\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$, bounded loss/contrast $\ell$, an i.i.d. sample, and a function class $\mathcal F$.

record.title: Large sets with limited tube occupancy: determine admissible dimension pairs
record.statement:
Determine the set of pairs $(\beta,\gamma)$ for which there exists a set $E\subseteq B$ with $0<\mathcal H^\beta(E)<\infty$ such that

$$
\sup_{r>0}\ \sup_{\substack{T\text{ an }r\text{-tube}}}\frac{\mathcal H^\beta(T\cap E)}{r^\gamma}<\infty.
$$

Here $B$ is the unit ball in $\mathbb R^d$, an $r$-tube is the $r$-neighbourhood of a line in $\mathbb R^d$, and $\mathcal H^\beta$ denotes $\beta$-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2043), page 68. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Normality relations in unitary free-group liberation
record.statement: For a compact group $G\subset U_n$, determine whether the normality of the generators $u_{ij}$ should be included among the defining relations $R$ in the liberation construction $A=C^*(u_{ij}\mid R)$. The source notes that normality should be avoided for $G=U_n$ in order to obtain a Hopf algebra, whereas for the complex reflection groups $G=H_n^s$ it should be included for compatibility with Voiculescu’s free probability theory; the general appropriate choice of $R$ in the unitary case remains unresolved.

record.title: Forbidden-order-type Erdős–Szekeres problem
record.statement: Assume that all point sets are in general position in the plane. Two point configurations have the same order type if there is a one-to-one correspondence preserving the orientation of every triple; an order type $T$ contains an order type $S$ if a configuration in $T$ contains a subset belonging to $S$. For an integer $n\ge 3$, let $C_n$ denote the order type of the vertices of a convex $n$-gon. For a fixed order type $T$, define $F_T(n)$ to be the smallest integer $N_0$ such that every order type of size at least $N_0$ that does not contain $T$ necessarily contains $C_n$. Is $F_T(n)$ always bounded above by a polynomial function of $n$?

record.title: Tree-routing property for the concave symmetric VPN design problem
record.statement: Every instance of the concave symmetric Virtual Private Network Design (cVPND) problem, with a simple undirected connected graph $G=(V,E)$, edge-cost vector $c\in\mathbb{R}_+^E$, maximum cumulative-demand vector $b\in\mathbb{Z}_+^V$, and non-decreasing concave capacity-cost function $f$, has an optimal virtual private network whose capacity support—or, equivalently, the union of its selected terminal-pair paths—induces a tree in $G$.

record.title: A four-point positive-characteristic Hurwitz-number formula
record.statement:
Let $p>0$ be prime, and let $C_i=e_i$ be the conjugacy class of a single cycle in $S_p$ for $i=1,2,3,4$. Assume that $p$ does not divide any ramification index and that $\sum_{i=1}^{4} e_i=2p+2$. Then
\[
h_p(p;e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4)=h(p;e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4)-p.
\]
Here $h$ is the characteristic-zero Hurwitz number and $h_p$ is the maximum, over choices of four branch points, of the number of covers of the indicated ramification type in characteristic $p$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2008/54](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2492), page 9. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Explicit ampleness bounds for determinantal equations of secant varieties
record.statement: For an embedding $X\subset \mathbb{P}^r$ given by the complete linear series of a sufficiently ample line bundle, the report suggests that the homogeneous ideal of the $k$th secant variety $\operatorname{Sec}_k(X)$ is generated by the $(k+2)\times(k+2)$ minors of the matrix $A$ arising from a factorization of the embedding line bundle. Assuming this assertion, determine explicit bounds for “sufficiently ample” in this context.

record.title: Infinite-horizon zonal temperature LQR control problem
record.statement:
Find a control $u$ minimizing
$$J(u)=\int_{0}^{\infty}\left([\xi(t)-r(t)]^{2}+R[u(t)]^{2}\right)\,dt,$$
where $R>0$, $r(t)$ is the desired average temperature, and
$$\xi(t)=\int_{\Omega_c}d(x)T(t,x)\,dx+w(t),$$
subject to the thermal PDE
$$\frac{\partial T(t,x)}{\partial t}+v(t,x)\cdot\nabla T(t,x)=\frac{1}{\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Pr}}\Delta T(t,x)+b(x)u(t)+g(x)v(t).$$
For the discussion in the report, $r(t)=0$. Under suitable assumptions and appropriate boundary conditions, this is formulated as the abstract system $\dot z(t)=Az(t)+Bu(t)+Gv(t)$, $t>0$, $z(0)=z_0\in Z$, with $Z=L^2(\Omega)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/04](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3387), page 16. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Minimizing the bottom of the spectrum in the random displacement model
record.statement: For the random displacement Hamiltonian $H_\omega=-\Delta+V_\omega$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$, with $V_\omega(x)=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}q(x-i-\omega_i)$, where $q$ is reflection-symmetric, compactly supported in the unit cube centered at the origin and each displaced copy remains supported in the unit cube centered at $i$, determine the configuration of the single-site potentials minimizing the bottom of the spectrum. The minimizing configuration is obtained by squeezing the potentials into the corners where $2^d$ cells meet, while keeping each support inside its cell; denoting it by $\omega^{\min}$, the report states $E_0:=\inf\Sigma=\inf\sigma(H_{\omega^{\min}})$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3389), page 24. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Bounds for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a quadrilateral
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be a quadrilateral with side lengths $\ell_i$, $i=1,\ldots,4$, and diagonals of lengths $d_1$ and $d_2$ forming an angle $\theta\in(0,\pi/2]$, where $d_2$ is the length of the largest diagonal contained in $Q$. If $A$ denotes the area of $Q$, then
\[
\frac{2\pi^2}{A}+\frac{\pi^2}{4A^2}\bigl(d_2\sin\theta-d_1\bigr)^2\leq\lambda_1(Q)\leq\frac{\pi^2}{2A^2}\sum_{i=1}^4\ell_i^2.
\]
Equality holds in the lower bound for squares and in the upper bound for rectangles.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3389), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Units of n-parameter free product systems
record.statement: Given $n$ one-parameter free product systems $E_i^{*}$, form the $n$-parameter free product system $E_{(t_1,\c5,t_n)}:=E_1^{*}\ast\cdots\ast E_n^{*}$ and the associated $E_0$-semigroup obtained by taking the inductive limit over the reference vector. Determine whether this system has any nontrivial units; in particular, decide whether its only units are the trivial ones consisting of the reference vectors.

record.title: Auxiliary triplet design problem for nonlinear output regulation
record.statement:
Find, if possible, a triplet $\{L(\varphi),M,N(\varphi)\}$ such that the system
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot w&=s(w),\\
\dot z&=f\bigl(w,z,N(\chi)\bigr),\\
\dot\chi&=L(\chi)+M\bigl[q\bigl(w,z,N(\chi)\bigr)+\gamma(x)\bigr],\\
\dot x&=F(x)-G_0q\bigl(w,z,N(\chi)\bigr)
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
possesses a compact invariant set $\mathcal A$ which is locally exponentially stable, with a domain of attraction containing the set of all admissible initial conditions, and such that $N(\chi)$ and $h\bigl(w,z,N(\chi)\bigr)+\gamma(x)$ vanish on $\mathcal A$.

record.title: Optimal fixed-dimensional coarse space
record.statement:
For a positive-definite weak problem on a Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ or $\mathbb{R}^3$, with $V=H_0^1(\Omega)$ or $V=H^1(\Omega)$ and energy norm $\|u\|_a^2=a(u,u)$, given an integer $n_H$, find a subspace $V_H\subset V$ of dimension $n_H$ minimizing
\[
\sup_{u\in V}\frac{\inf_{v\in V_H}\|u-v\|_{L^2}^2}{\|u\|_a^2}.
\]
The report explains that, when the inverse of the differential operator is compact, the minimizing space is spanned by the eigenfunctions corresponding to the lowest $n_H$ eigenvalues.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3395), page 39. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Best-approximation property of the energy-minimizing sparse interpolation matrix
record.statement:
The report states the following theorem. Let $P$ be the unique solution of the energy minimization problem (1), with the prescribed sparsity pattern, and let $P^{\star}$ denote the ideal interpolation matrix. With
\[
\|\!\|\!\|X\|\!\|\!\|_{A}:=\operatorname{trace}(X^{T}AX),
\]
one has
\[
\|\!\|\!\|P^{\star}-P\|\!\|\!\|_{A}
 =\min_{Q}\|\!\|\!\|P^{\star}-Q\|\!\|\!\|_{A},
\]
where the minimum is over all matrices $Q$ having the same prescribed sparsity as $P$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/12](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3395), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Classification of torus-invariant prime ideals in the quantum Grassmannian
record.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $q\in k\setminus\{0\}$ be not a root of unity, and fix integers $0<m\le n$. Let $A=\mathcal O_q(G_{m,n})$ be the quantum Grassmannian, and let $H=(k^*)^n$ act naturally on $A$. The classification problem is to determine $H\text{-}\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the set of $H$-invariant prime ideals of $A$. The report states that there is a natural one-to-one correspondence between $H\text{-}\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_q(G_{m,n}))$ and the Cauchon diagrams fitting in an $m\times(n-m)$ rectangular Young diagram, where each box is black or white and, whenever a box is black, either all boxes above it or all boxes to its left are black.

record.title: Uniform density-independent bounds and bandwidth selection in multivariate density estimation
record.statement: For the empirical process \(\xi_w(t)=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(w(t,X_i)-\mathbb{E}w(t,X)\bigr)\), find a uniform upper bound for \(\|\xi_w\|_{s,\tau}\) that is independent of the unknown density \(f\), and construct such a bound using only the observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\). record.title: Characterization of exact $\[1$-recovery under sign restrictions
record.statement:
Given a matrix $A\in\ R^{m\\times n}$ with $m<n$, subsets $P_{+},P_{-}\subseteq\robrace{1,\ldots,n}$ satisfying $P_{+}\cap P_{-}=\varnothing$, and an integer sparsity level $s$, determine whether, whenever the true signal $w\in\ R^n$ is $s$-sparse and satisfies $w_i\geq0$ for $i\in P_{+}$ and $w_i\leq0$ for $i\in P_{-}$, the noiseless sign-constrained $\[1$-recovery problem

$$\[hat w'\in\operatorname{argmin}_{x}\robrace{\Vert x\Vert_1:Ax=Aw,\ x_i\geq0\ \forall i\in P_{+},\ x_i\leq0\ \forall i\in P_{-}\robrace}$$

recovers $w$ exactly.

record.title: Gluing problem for blocks of finite groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ with $p\mid |G|$, and let $b$ be a block of $kG$. Fix a maximal $b$-Brauer pair $(P,e_P)$, and for each $Q\le P$ let $e_Q$ be the unique block of $kC_G(Q)$ such that $(Q,e_Q)\le (P,e_P)$. Let $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{(P,e_P)}(G,b)$ be the saturated fusion system on $P$ determined by $b$, and let $\mathcal F^c$ be its full subcategory of $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups. With $\mathcal S(\mathcal F^c)$, $A_2$, and the exact sequence in Theorem 2.2 as defined in the report, the block $b$ determines an element $\alpha_0\in H^0([\mathcal S(\mathcal F^c)],A_2)$. Find $\alpha\in H^2(\mathcal F^c,k^\times)$ such that $d(\alpha)=\alpha_0$.

record.title: Toroidalization in higher dimensions
record.statement:
Suppose that \(\Phi:X\to Y\) is a dominant morphism of varieties over a field of characteristic zero. Construct a commutative diagram
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
X_1 & \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_1\ } & Y_1\\
\downarrow && \downarrow\\
X & \xrightarrow{\ \Phi\ } & Y
\end{array}
\]
such that the vertical arrows are products of monoidal transforms (blowups of nonsingular subvarieties) and \(\Phi_1:X_1\to Y_1\) is toroidal. Here toroidal means that there are simple normal-crossing divisors \(D_X\) on \(X\) and \(D_Y\) on \(Y\), with \(\Phi^{-1}(D_Y)=D_X\), such that, at every point, the morphism is formally isomorphic to a morphism of toric varieties, equivalently is locally monomial with respect to these divisors.

record.title: Computing Frobenius conjugacy classes from a polynomial and its Galois group
record.statement: Suppose $f(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ has degree $n$, with roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$, splitting field $K=\mathbb{Q}(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$, and Galois group $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q})\subset S_n$. record.title: Strict lowering of the Be-like $J=1$ multiconfiguration energy below the ${}^{3}P_{1}$ sector
record.statement:

record.title: Formal normal form and Stokes filtration of an exponentially twisted Gauss–Manin connection
record.statement:
Let \b[?25l$(E,\nabla)$ be a free $\mathcal O_\Delta[x]$-module equipped with a meromorphic connection on $\Delta\times\mathbb A^1$, with logarithmic poles along $S\cup(\Delta\times\{\infty\})$. \]

record.title: Optimal domain assumptions for positivity of hinged plates
record.statement:
For the hinged-plate problem
\[
\Delta^2 v=f\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad v=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega,\qquad \Delta v-(1-\sigma)\kappa v_n=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega,
\]
where \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2\) is bounded and convex, \(-1<\sigma<1\), and \(f\in L^2(\Omega)\), determine whether the assumptions on \(\Omega\) in Theorem 1—especially \(\partial\Omega\in C^{2,1}\)—are optimal, and whether the theorem’s positivity conclusion remains valid under weaker or otherwise improved domain hypotheses. The conclusion in question is that the minimizer/unique weak solution satisfies \(f\ge 0\), \(f\not\equiv0\Rightarrow v_\sigma(x)>c_f\,d(x,\partial\Omega)\) for some \(c_f>0\).

record.title: Minimum output Rényi entropy additivity counterexamples
record.statement:
For a given $p\ge 1$, do there exist two quantum channels $\Phi_1,\Phi_2$ such that

$H_p^{\mathrm{min}}(\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2)<H_p^{\mathrm{min}}(\Phi_1)+H_p^{\mathrm{min}}(\Phi_2)$?

Here a quantum channel is a linear completely positive trace-preserving map between finite matrix algebras, and $H_p^{\mathrm{min}}(\Phi)$ is the minimum, over input density matrices, of the order-$p$ Rényi entropy of the eigenvalues of the output. The report answers affirmatively: the statement was proved by Hayden and Winter for $p>1$ and by Hastings for $p=1$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/13](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4214), page 30. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Bandwidth selection for kernel density estimators
record.statement:
Given an i.i.d. sample $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ from a density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, a kernel $K$ with $\int K(x)\,dx=1$, and the family of kernel estimators $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{H})=\{\widehat f_h:h\in\mathcal{H}\}$ indexed by bandwidth vectors in $\mathcal{H}=\prod_{i=1}^d[h^{(i)}_{\min},h^{(i)}_{\max}]$, the bandwidth-selection problem is to construct a measurable choice $\widehat h\in\mathcal{H}$ such that $\widehat f=\widehat f_{\widehat h}$ satisfies an $L^s$-risk oracle inequality. The report states that such a choice exists, with
$$
R_s[\widehat f;f]\leq \bigl(C(s)+3\lVert K\rVert_1\bigr)\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_s[\widehat f_h;f]+\delta_{n,s},\qquad \forall f\in\mathcal{F},
$$
and gives the corresponding remainder bounds for $s\geq2$ and $s\in[1,2)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2010/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4217), page 19. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

The report presents such Giambelli formulas, including raising-operator formulas for symplectic Grassmannians and formulas for type $A$ and type $C$ partial flag varieties.
